36.0.0.en: 1- The utterance of the transgression of the wicked is within my heart: that there is no fear of God before his eyes.

36.0.1.en: The utterance: a groaning, or a sigh, or an aching in the heart.

36.0.2.en: 1- David's heart aches when he looks at the sins of the wicked, which all result from their neglect of the fear of God; for since they do not fear Him, they rush easily into any sin.

36.0.3.en: 2- When the wicked neglect the fear of God they fall into the fear of men, so they care for the outward appearance of their lives, while their insides are evil; that is, they become hypocrites and pretenders.

36.0.4.en: 3- Because the wicked do not fear God, they neglect His commandments, and this makes it easy for them to fall into sin.

36.0.5.en: 4- David's fatherhood appears in this verse; not only toward his obedient, righteous children, but also his fatherhood toward the wicked, so his heart aches for them, and he longs that they return to God, that they may fear Him and keep away from every sin.

36.1.0.en: 2- For he flattereth himself to himself concerning the finding out of his iniquity and the hating of it.

36.1.1.en: He flattereth himself: that is, he deceives himself and honors himself beyond what he deserves.

36.1.2.en: 1- One of the characteristics of the wicked is that he is deceitful; he deceives others, but the harder thing is that he deceives even himself, deluding himself that he is upright and behaves well, and consequently he keeps entirely away from repentance, since he does not feel his sin; so how can he repent of it?

36.1.3.en: 2- The wicked man flatters himself because of his pride; he does not want to imagine the truth, nor does he accept it, for his pride is built on delusions with which he has deceived himself.

36.1.4.en: 3- The wicked man justifies to himself the evils and iniquities he commits, and likewise his hatred of others, so he imagines that his iniquities are not evil, and pictures to himself that his hatred of others is merely not feeling at ease with them, and that the others are the cause of that.

36.1.5.en: 4- The wicked man also deludes himself that he hates evil and loves what is upright, and by this he finds in himself no sin or hatred to repent of.

36.1.6.en: 5- The wicked man begins by justifying himself in small sins, then justifies himself in greater sins, until he does the greatest evils without realizing it, because he is far from repentance; thus he does not hate his iniquity, because he does not feel it.

36.2.0.en: 3- The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit: he hath left off to be wise, and to do good.

36.2.1.en: 1- The wicked man has made deceit permissible, and as he continued deceiving himself and deceiving others, he believed the evil he says, so he moved away from the truth and from wisdom, and lost discernment.

36.2.2.en: 2- The wicked man's departing from wisdom is by his own will, because he deceived himself and so kept it far from understanding and upright conduct.

36.2.3.en: 3- If the wicked man is immersed in his sins and departs from wisdom, he departs from everything good and from helping others, because he does not feel for them; so how can he help them or do good with them? He is selfish, occupied with himself and his pride, and consequently he loses God's mercy and the love of others for him.

36.2.4.en: 4- The wicked man's continuing in deceit will stop the work of the Holy Spirit in him, so his heart will not be convicted, nor will he repent of his sins, and he remains far from God.

36.3.0.en: 4- He deviseth iniquity upon his bed; he standeth in a way that is not good; he refuseth not evil.

36.3.1.en: 1- When the wicked man enters the place where he will sleep, instead of examining himself and repenting like the rest of mankind, he thinks about evil, so he remains deceived and far from God.

36.3.2.en: 2- Since the wicked man has lost his discernment, he no longer keeps away from evil, but on the contrary stands in the way of evil and sits in the seat of the scornful and the sinners, and consequently goes further in his sins and remains in his error.

36.3.3.en: 3- Because of the wicked man's great deceiving of himself, and his words full of iniquity and deceit, he loses his ability to resist evil, so he falls easily into any sin, and thus becomes a slave of Satan, who controls him as he sees fit.

36.3.4.en: 4- The wicked man in secret thinks about evil, so he surrenders to it inwardly, and it becomes easy for him to do wicked deeds by day, because he is premeditating the doing of evil.

36.3.5.en: 5- The wicked deeds that the wicked man does lead him to think about evil when he lies down to sleep. Man reaps at night the fruit of his deeds during the day. But for the righteous the night is an opportunity for repentance, prayer and praise.

36.3.6.en: Look at the hideousness of your sins and their effects on you, that you may reject them by repentance and take refuge in God in the sacrament of confession, that He may forgive them for you and cleanse you, and you come out with a new nature inclined to the love of God and of others.

36.4.0.en: 5- Thy mercy, O LORD, is in the heavens; and thy faithfulness reacheth unto the clouds.

36.4.1.en: 1- God's mercy is great and cannot be measured because it is in heaven; it is unlimited, and man cannot enumerate it. Therefore man's heart is reassured that however many his sins, God's mercies are wider and cover them.

36.4.2.en: 2- God's mercies are higher than the thoughts of men, for He seeks the salvation of their souls, and not merely the supplying of their material needs; therefore mercy may allow the chastening of the children of God for a time, until they return to Him.

36.4.3.en: 3- God's mercies and faithfulness are higher than man's understanding, and they are hidden in the clouds; therefore it is fitting for man to believe in God and submit to Him, and let Him give him the blessings in their season.

36.4.4.en: 4- God's faithfulness is in His promises to mankind. Just as He promised Noah not to destroy the world again with a flood by the appearance of the sign of the rainbow in the sky when the sky rains heavily, so too God's promises are many, protecting His children and reassuring them, for God wants all to be saved, and seeks all sinners that they may repent.

36.4.5.en: 5- God's mercy is in those who walk a heavenly walk, for it is in the heavens, that is, in the saints and the heavenly children of God in their life on earth.

36.5.0.en: 6- Thy justice is like the mountains of God; thy judgments are a great deep: O LORD, thou savest man and beast.

36.5.1.en: 1- God's justice is firm and strong like a mountain; it does not waver or change like the justice of men, that is, God's principles are fixed, and He cannot be deceived, and He is the searcher of hearts and reins. This reassures the righteous, frightens the wicked, and calls all of us to repentance.

36.5.2.en: 2- God's judgments and commandments are very deep like the depths of the sea, and everyone who contemplates them is satisfied and rejoices and lives by them, and so tastes the Kingdom while on earth.

36.5.3.en: 3- God's judgments do not conflict with His justice, for He has mercy on sinners and is long-suffering toward them until they repent, so they are not punished by divine justice.

36.5.4.en: 4- God's judgments and commandments are too deep for man to understand; he grasps only a little of them, and the solution is to submit to them and let God order our lives by His good will.

36.5.5.en: 5- God's deep judgments, like the deep sea, testify to His greatness, for He is unlimited in His wisdom; therefore how beautiful it is for man to keep God's commandments and repeat them, so that they become a source of blessings and constant satisfaction for his soul.

36.5.6.en: 6- God in His love cares for His children, and likewise for the rest of the creatures for their sake, so He saves, that is, He cares for the beasts, the plants and all creatures for the sake of man. God cares for His children and for the whole world for their sake.

36.6.0.en: 7- How precious is thy mercy, O God! therefore the children of men take refuge under the shadow of thy wings.

36.6.1.en: 1- God's mercy is greater than any other mercy, because His mercy is unlimited, generous in its giving, and suits every person; for it is that which created man, so it understands him, and is able to cover all mankind, especially as the word "God" means the God of the whole world, and not only the children of Israel, who mostly use the word "LORD."

36.6.2.en: 2- Because God's mercy is wide and distinguished, all the children of men take refuge in it, to protect them from every evil, forgive them their sins, and care for all their needs.

36.6.3.en: 3- What is meant by the children of men are the believers in God, who seek God and trust in His protection.

36.6.4.en: 4- God's wings represent protection; as the hen protects her chicks under her wings, and as the two cherubim cover with their wings the cover of the Ark of the Covenant, which is called the mercy seat; the two wings signify God's fatherhood, His care and His love for the children of men, and they also signify the Old and New Testaments.

36.7.0.en: 8- They are satisfied with the fatness of thy house, and thou givest them drink from the river of thy pleasures.

36.7.1.en: 1- God's care appears in His concern for the needs of His children; He satisfies them and feeds them, not only with material food and drink but rather with the spiritual; for they hunger and thirst after righteousness, and they are satisfied with His unlimited love.

36.7.2.en: 2- God feeds His children generously; He does not give them ordinary food, but rich food, which makes them need nothing of all that is in the world.

36.7.3.en: 3- The house of God is the Church, and its fatness is its holy sacraments, which surpass the mind. David, in the spirit of prophecy, sees the Church of the New Testament and union with God through its sacraments.

36.7.4.en: 4- The river of grace is the Holy Spirit, who works in the being of those who believe in Him through the sacraments, the means of grace and the manifold gifts, and so waters all.

36.7.5.en: 5- The river of grace signifies the water and the blood that came out of the side of Christ on the Cross, to water all who believe in Him.

36.8.0.en: 9- For with thee is the fountain of life: in thy light shall we see light.

36.8.1.en: 1- The Holy Trinity appears in this verse: in his saying "with thee," that is, the Father, and "the fountain of life" is the Son, and "the light" is the Holy Spirit. God in His three hypostases cares for the man who believes in Him.

36.8.2.en: 2- The light also signifies the word of God, which enlightens the eyes of our hearts amid the error and evil of the world.

36.8.3.en: 3- The light of God signifies the Incarnation of Christ, by whom we see the light, that is, the Father; for "No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him" (Jn 1:18). We see this verse repeated in the New Testament in speaking of Christ, "In him was life; and the life was the light of men" (Jn 1:4).

36.9.0.en: 10- O continue thy mercy unto them that know thee; and thy justice to the upright in heart.

36.9.1.en: 1- Those who know God believe in Him, and know that He is righteous and holy, so they repent of their sins before His holiness, and as they humble themselves God pours out on them His forgiveness and mercies.

36.9.2.en: 2- When God continues His mercy to those who know Him, this helps them to grow in the knowledge of God and to hold fast to Him, so God's mercies upon them increase, and thus God's mercy leads to spiritual growth. And when man grows He pours out on him more mercies.

36.9.3.en: 3- God's mercies cover all mankind, like His sun that shines on the righteous and the wicked, and His air, and His water ... but those who know God take notice, appreciate these mercies and thank the Lord for them; therefore God's mercies continue upon them and become more varied than for those who do not appreciate these mercies.

36.9.4.en: 4- Whoever walks in uprightness wishes that God's justice would prevail, so that evil may not increase, but that all may know that the upright is rewarded and the wicked is punished. Justice does right by the upright and blesses them.

36.9.5.en: 5- The upright in heart is a person who believed in God, relied on Him and kept His commandments, and consequently accepts His will and does not murmur at any affliction; therefore divine justice does right by him and rewards him.

36.10.0.en: 11- Let not the foot of pride come against me, and let not the hand of the wicked remove me.

36.10.1.en: 12- There are the workers of iniquity fallen: they are cast down, and shall not be able to rise.

36.10.2.en: 1- David, who walks in uprightness and lives with God, wishes that the proud Satan would not attack him and make him walk in the way of pride; therefore he said "the foot of pride."

36.10.3.en: 2- As long as David walks in the way of goodness and lives with God, he asks that the hand of Satan, that is, the works of the wicked, be kept away from him, so that he is not moved from his upright way and the doing of good.

36.10.4.en: 3- David asks that he not walk by his own will, that is, with his foot, in the way of weeping, and that outward wars not be extended to him, that is, the hand of the wicked, to remove him from God's way.

36.10.5.en: 4- Whoever does not humble himself and walks in the way of pride, or responds to the works of the wicked, will fall into sin and be separated from God, as Adam did in the garden of Eden when he wanted to become like God.

36.10.6.en: 5- If man continues in the way of pride and wicked deeds, the devil will triumph over him, and his end will be destruction and eternal torment, where he falls and cannot rise. What is meant by the word "there" is that far from God is the fall, and then eternal torment.

36.10.7.en: Endure the labors of keeping the commandment so as to walk in uprightness, and then God's mercies will pour out upon you, and His justice will keep you to a happy eternal life, and you will escape all the devil's plots.

36.10.8.en: The recompense of the righteous and the wicked. By David. "Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity" ... (v. 1) Introduction:

36.10.10.en: 2- When it was written: in the last part of David's life, that is, about three years before his death, for it carries the sum of his experience of God's dealing with the righteous and the wicked.

36.10.11.en: 3- It encourages the righteous in any afflictions that meet them, so that they are not troubled by the temporary success of the wicked.

36.10.12.en: 4- It is one of the Messianic psalms, for it speaks of Christ and the blessings of the Church of the New Testament.

36.10.13.en: 5- This psalm is didactic, for it is full of counsels, and resembles Psalms (73, 94), and also resembles the books of Job, Proverbs and Jesus son of Sirach.

36.10.14.en: 6- This psalm is arranged according to the Hebrew alphabet, meaning that every verse, or two verses, begins with one of the letters of the alphabet, and the forty verses fall under twenty-two Hebrew letters. This is the third of the psalms arranged according to the Hebrew alphabet.

36.10.15.en: 7- This psalm is not found in the Agpeya.

37.0.0.en: 1- Fret not thyself because of evildoers, neither be thou envious against the workers of iniquity.

37.0.1.en: 2- For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb.

37.0.2.en: 1- These are the first two counsels that David gives to the children of God, that they may stand firm in the upright faith, and they are the first of the eight counsels that he sets out in this passage. He counsels the righteous not to be dazzled by the temporary success of the wicked, and not to fall into jealousy and envy.

37.0.3.en: 2- Jealousy and envy are two sins into which the prophet David warns us not to fall, whether toward the wicked or toward any person, because they show that we are not content and satisfied with God, and also our lack of love for the others whom we envy.

37.0.4.en: 3- The success of the wicked is temporary, and he likens them to grass or green herb, which grows quickly in the ground, then dries up and vanishes before the heat of the sun. But the righteous the Holy Bible likens to the palm tree with deep roots, which flourishes and blossoms, and to the trees of Lebanon, and all strong trees with a deep root (Ps 92:13).

37.0.5.en: 4- The success of the wicked does not last long, and even if it continues throughout life, it ends on the Day of Judgment, where there is no rest for them but torment, for the hypocrites will not stand in the judgment (Ps 1:5).

37.0.6.en: 5- The material success of the wicked is accompanied by turmoil in the heart, so they cannot have inward peace, as the prophet Isaiah said, "There is no peace, saith the LORD, unto the wicked" (Isa 48:22).

37.0.7.en: 6- The likening of the wicked and those occupied with the world to grass and herb is used in the Holy Bible in both Testaments (Isa 40:6-8; Jas 1:11).

37.1.0.en: 3- Trust in the LORD, and do good; dwell in the land and feed on faithfulness.

37.1.1.en: 1- The third counsel is reliance on God. Whoever believes in God knows that He has perfect power and unlimited love, and consequently He is the only One on whom man relies with all confidence, and so receives rest and peace.

37.1.2.en: 2- Whoever keeps away from attachment to the material things of the earth and the success of the wicked, so that he neither envies them nor is jealous of them, finds it easy to fix his gaze on God, so he sees His beauty and power and relies on Him.

37.1.3.en: 3- If man clings to God and relies on Him, he becomes positive, and so he is able to carry out the fourth counsel, which is doing good. For whoever loves God and relies on Him is able to love people and strive to serve them.

37.1.4.en: 4- If man is occupied with doing good, God helps him, so he feels God's love and care, and increases in doing good, and thus grows in the love of others; for he is gradually freed from his selfishness, and becomes a flame of love that lights and warms the whole world.

37.1.5.en: 5- The natural result that the one who keeps away from jealousy and envy, relies on God, and is open in love toward others receives is that God grants him settlement in the land, so that he dwells in it, but on condition that he carries out the fifth counsel, which is faithfulness in all his works on earth and his dealings with others, so that he is settled in his life and works, and is faithful in cultivating the land or fulfilling his duties toward others, and God is pleased with him and blesses him.

37.1.6.en: 6- Dwelling in the land may mean - as St. Jerome said - dwelling in the land of the living, that is, the Church, so that he is nourished by its holy sacraments and the means of grace, on condition of faithfulness in carrying out God's commandments.

37.1.7.en: 7- Dwelling in the land can also mean dwelling in eternity, that is, receiving the eternal inheritance for those who were faithful in their life on earth; for the one who is faithful over a few things, that is, his earthly life, God makes ruler over many things, that is, his eternal life (Mt 25:21).

37.2.0.en: 4- Delight thyself also in the LORD; and he shall give thee the desires of thine heart.

37.2.1.en: 1- The sixth result is delighting, rejoicing and enjoying God, and it is built on the previous counsels; for whoever lives in fellowship with God and relies on Him, does good and is faithful in everything, God's mercies and gifts pour out upon him, so he thanks God and rejoices in fellowship with Him. What is meant by joy and delight is that man be aware of God's gifts, and look at His beloved Person, so that he rejoices in Him, that is, rejoices in being with God and enjoys His gifts.

37.2.2.en: 2- We notice here in this counsel that David moves us from delighting in God's gifts and relying on Him to discovering God's beauty and contemplating Him, and this is the true joy and complete delight.

37.2.3.en: 3- The result of rejoicing in fellowship with God is that God gives those who love Him the desires of their hearts, and he says here the desires of the heart, and not the requests of the mouth, that is, what man wishes, even if he does not utter it. The wishes of the heart are deeper than the wishes of the lips, but God, the rich and generous Giver, gives His children the desire of their hearts. The Apostle Paul asked for healing from the thorn in the flesh, that he might be able to serve God with all freedom, and God did not answer his request for healing, but He gave him the desire of his heart, so he preached more than all the Apostles, and wrote more books of the Holy Bible than all.

37.3.0.en: 5- Commit thy way unto the LORD; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass.

37.3.1.en: 6- And he shall bring forth thy righteousness as the light, and thy right as the noonday.

37.3.2.en: 1- Here he confirms the third counsel, which is reliance on God and committing life to Him, so that God Himself leads man's way, guides him in all his steps, and protects him from stumbling, until He brings him to the Kingdom.

37.3.3.en: 2- When man believes in God and commits his life to Him, God brings all his affairs to pass uprightly; that is, He works in his life, so he is able to carry out God's commandments, behaves well, and feels God's being with him, so his heart rejoices in God's companionship throughout his life.

37.3.4.en: 3- The wicked are troubled by the righteousness of the righteous, so they fight him, accuse him falsely, and wrong him with bad words, and the righteous endures all this for God's sake, and then God intervenes, and the righteousness of the righteous appears like the light after the darkness of the bad words that the wicked said about him; that is, God - on whom the righteous relied - declares, "This is my son, and I am with him," and this divine glorification is a pledge of the glory of the Kingdom of Heaven.

37.3.5.en: 4- If the wicked take away the right of the righteous, whether his material rights or his dignity, God intervenes after this and declares his right, and blesses him with many blessings that are strong, as the rays of the sun are strong at noonday. God rewards the righteous for his endurance, as He appeared to the righteous Abraham, who left everything for His sake, and that at noonday, and was host to God with the two angels (Gen 18:1), and as Joseph honored his brothers with a delicious meal at noonday, showing them his love (Gen 43:16), and as Christ declared His perfect love for mankind when He was hung on the Cross to redeem them at noonday (Lk 23:33, 44).

37.4.0.en: 7- Wait for the LORD and be patient for him, and fret not thyself because of him who prospereth in his way, because of the man who bringeth wicked devices to pass.

37.4.1.en: 1- The seventh counsel is patience. When afflictions follow one another and the wicked man goes further in his wrongs toward the righteous, the righteous grows weary, but God counsels him through David's mouth to be patient and wait for God's salvation; for God watches everything, and will surely intervene and reward the righteous, and indeed during the affliction He supports him, giving him peace and establishing him in the upright way.

37.4.2.en: 2- In order for the righteous to be able to be patient he must hold fast to God's commandments and promises, so that he is not shaken by Satan's casting of doubts upon him, and does not fret over the success of the wicked, because they do evil and plots in order to achieve their successes.

37.4.3.en: 3- In order for man to be able to be patient he needs divine help, so he lifts up his heart in prayer at all times to receive help at every time, and his heart is comforted during the affliction.

37.4.4.en: 4- Patience means that man accepts afflictions with contentment and thanksgiving and does not murmur. The word "be patient" in the Hebrew original means "be silent and do not murmur," so God rejoices in his faith and steadfastness and rewards him for his patience.

37.4.5.en: 5- Whoever waits for the Lord does not set Him a time to intervene in his life, but trusts in God's wisdom and only waits for Him, as Judith declared to the people of her city and reproached them that they had not been patient for God, confident of His salvation; and because of her faith God intervened and rescued her country from the enemies by her killing Holofernes, the commander of the armies of the Assyrians (Jdt 8:11-14).

37.5.0.en: 8- Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.

37.5.1.en: 1- The eighth and last counsel is not to be angry; for anger means murmuring against God and against people, in addition to wronging others and man's losing his peace, so he is far from God and cannot pray with purity, and loses his fellowship with God.

37.5.2.en: 2- If man is lax with the sin of anger it increases and turns into severe anger, which is wrath, and if man does not restrain himself from wrath it turns into the doing of evil, like the rest of the wicked. Therefore the sin must be cut off at its beginning, which is the thought of anger.

37.5.3.en: 3- God gave man His commandments and promised to help him fulfill them however heavy they may seem, so why should man be angry and not continue his striving? God did not promise us the easy way and the wide gate, and therefore we should accept afflictions and not be angry.

37.6.0.en: 9- For evildoers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon the LORD, they shall inherit the earth.

37.6.1.en: 10- For yet a little while, and the wicked shall not be: yea, thou shalt diligently consider his place, and it shall not be.

37.6.2.en: 11- But the meek shall inherit the earth; and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

37.6.3.en: 1- The wicked are cut off from before God, that is, their occupation with material things and the doing of evils is temporary, and after a little while they are not, that is, their life on earth ends, and they are removed far from God and cast into eternal torment.

37.6.4.en: 2- The righteous inherit the earth, and David repeats the inheriting of the earth in this psalm six times. What is meant by the earth - as we said - is the Promised Land, that is, the land of Canaan, and likewise the righteous enjoy their life on earth because God is with them and blesses them.

37.6.5.en: 3- The earth is also meant to be the Church of the New Testament, the land of the living, where the believers receive the sacraments of the Church and the means of grace, and enjoy even more fellowship with God.

37.6.6.en: 4- The earth is also meant to be the new earth, or the heavenly Jerusalem, which is the eternal inheritance, so the believers remain in fellowship with God and enjoy seeing Him in the Kingdom.

37.6.7.en: 5- The meek are those who live with God, so He gives them His inward peace, and they are not troubled by any material gain or loss. This peace is abundant in their hearts, and increases in the Church of the New Testament, then is completed in the Kingdom of Heaven, where it is abundant without limits, that is, they live in peace forever.

37.6.8.en: 6- The meek are the righteous who meet many afflictions and endure them for God's sake, so He gives them His inward peace, and they are approved before Him, and He also gives them eternal life.

37.6.9.en: 7- The abundance of peace is for the meek however much afflictions surround them, because the unlimited God is the source of peace, and He gives it generously to His children. And peace increases as they grow spiritually, until it is completed in the Kingdom.

37.6.10.en: The way of righteousness is the way of happiness, so hold fast to it and keep God's commandments, and you will receive His blessings, and even possess God in your heart and taste the Kingdom while you are on earth, and then you will make light of afflictions and not be troubled by them.

37.7.0.en: 12- The wicked plotteth against the just, and gnasheth upon him with his teeth.

37.7.1.en: 1- The wicked man has plotted evil against the righteous since the beginning of creation; this is what Satan did with Adam and Eve, then made them fall, and Cain did with Abel, and it continues until now.

37.7.2.en: 2- If the wicked man fails to harm the righteous he is enraged, so he gnashes on him with his teeth, that is, grinds his teeth in rage, because the righteous held fast to God and His commandments, and so escaped from the hand of the devil.

37.7.3.en: 3- These evils that the wicked man stirs up against the righteous are temporary in this life, but God removes them from the righteous for many periods, and then removes them completely in the Kingdom of Heaven.

37.8.0.en: 13- The LORD laugheth at him: for he seeth that his day is coming!

37.8.1.en: 1- The Lord laughs at the wicked man who devises conspiracies against the righteous, trusts in his power and wrongs others, because all this is temporary and will soon end with the end of his life, and also the Lord can end him by exposing his plans and protecting the righteous from him. God is stronger than the wicked man, but He is long-suffering toward him, that perhaps he may repent.

37.8.2.en: 2- As the wicked man laughs at the righteous and harms him, or tries to harm him, God laughs at the wicked man and stops his evil, and even ends his life, so he goes to eternal torment; as the wicked man does, so it is done to him. What is meant by these words is that every person should take heed and not do evil.

37.8.3.en: 3- The coming day is the Day of Judgment, where the wicked man is judged for every evil thought, word or deed; therefore the righteous who fears God and remembers the judgment keeps away from evil and keeps God's commandments.

37.9.0.en: 14- The wicked have drawn out the sword, and have bent their bow, to cast down the poor and needy, to slay the upright in their way.

37.9.1.en: The upright in their way: those who walk in the upright way of the Lord.

37.9.2.en: 1- The sword and the bow are two instruments of war that show the conspiracies of the wicked against the poor righteous man, who is without weapon. This shows the extent of the wicked's injustice and cruelty, and their exploiting the righteous man's material weakness, so they conspire against him.

37.9.3.en: 2- The sword represents the visible instrument of war with which the wicked man attacks the poor man, and the bow represents the hidden instrument of war with which the wicked man throws arrows from afar, and they strike the poor man; the wicked man uses all wicked means to destroy the poor man. Therefore their punishment from God is severe.

37.9.4.en: 3- The righteousness of the children of God provokes and exposes the evil of the wicked, so instead of repenting and returning to uprightness they are enraged, and attack the righteous to get rid of him, so that their evil is not exposed by his holiness.

37.9.5.en: 4- The wonder is that God returns the evils of the wicked upon their heads, so He protects the righteous, and the conspiracies return upon the wicked, so their swords strike their hearts, that is, destroy them, and if they remain alive their hearts are tormented by evil. And God shows the weakness of their bows, so they are broken, that is, their conspiracies fail. God means by this to establish the righteous in their faith and to call the wicked to repentance; but whoever does not repent, his evil harms him, as Haman perished and was hanged on the gallows on which he wanted to hang Mordecai (Esth 7:10), and as King Saul perished in the war, he who wanted to destroy David (1 Sam 31:4), and as Absalom perished and died in the war, having wanted to destroy his father David (2 Sam 18:15).

37.10.0.en: 16- A little that a righteous man hath is better than the riches of many wicked.

37.10.1.en: 17- For the arms of the wicked shall be broken: but the LORD upholdeth the righteous.

37.10.2.en: Arms: plural of forearm, which is the arm.

37.10.3.en: Upholdeth: supports and strengthens, that is, the one who strengthens man's upper arm, which is his arm.

37.10.4.en: 1- Although the righteous man possesses little, yet by God's blessing it suffices him and overflows; but as for the wicked man, however great his wealth, he does not benefit from it, but his heart remains troubled and he does not enjoy his life.

37.10.5.en: 2- The power of the wicked is temporary, and their arms are broken, that is, they are unable to work, whether during their life on earth or by the end of this life, so they find no rest in eternity, because they are cast into eternal torment.

37.10.6.en: 3- God upholds and supports the righteous; therefore their power is mighty and without limit, because it is from God Himself, so no one can overcome them as long as they are with God, as Pharaoh and his mighty army were broken before the children of Israel by the ten plagues, and then by drowning in the Red Sea.

37.10.7.en: 4- God supports His children, not only in this life, that they may stand firm in faith in Him and keep His commandments, but He supports them forever in the Kingdom, where He lets them enjoy His great glory.

37.11.0.en: 18- The LORD knoweth the days of the perfect: and their inheritance shall be for ever.

37.11.1.en: 19- They shall not be ashamed in the evil time: and in the days of famine they shall be satisfied.

37.11.3.en: 1- The perfect are those who loved God, and realize that they are the image of God and His likeness, so they imitate Him in His perfection, in spiritual striving, rising above material things and honor, and occupied with being with God and doing good with every person.

37.11.4.en: 2- God knows everything, so why does he mention here that He knows the days of the perfect? What is meant is that He is concerned with caring for the days of the perfect, that is, He looks after the life of His children who strive on the way of perfection, for He loves them because they imitate Him.

37.11.5.en: 3- God knows the days of the perfect, that is, He notices their striving and their labor on the way of perfection, and prepares for them a great place in the Kingdom, to compensate them in it for their labors on earth. This is the eternal inheritance.

37.11.6.en: 4- God cares for His perfect children during afflictions, which are the days of evil and famine, and it is not necessary that He remove the affliction from them, but He is able to keep them within the affliction, as He kept Elijah during the famine (1 Kgs 17:4, 9).

37.11.7.en: 5- During the days of evil and famine God satisfies His children spiritually, so they are not troubled by the lack of food or the pressures of life, though these pass over them, but their occupation with God gives them peace and rest, so they pass through the affliction quietly.

37.12.0.en: 20- But the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the LORD shall be as the splendor of the pastures: they are consumed; like smoke they are consumed.

37.12.1.en: 1- The wicked are the enemies of God, who keep away from His commandments because of their occupation with doing evil. Because they are separated from God and hold fast to evil, their end must be destruction.

37.12.2.en: 2- He likens the wicked to herbs that grow quickly and dry up and wither quickly too. They represent the superficial life, and have no fruit, therefore they quickly perish, and have no enjoyment of God, even if their life on earth is long; but in eternity they perish, that is, their material enjoyment ends with the end of dominion, and then they are in torment forever.

37.12.3.en: 3- He also likens the wicked to smoke; for although the fire appears great, it too goes out, and leaves nothing but the smoke that rises up and fills a large space, then scatters and vanishes.

37.12.4.en: 4- Even if the wicked are found in the pastures, which signify the churches, they are merely herbage that quickly perishes because their life is superficial; but the pastures are filled with flocks of cattle, that is, the churches are filled with their children who are full of spiritual richness and enjoy fellowship with God.

37.13.0.en: 21- The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again: but the righteous is compassionate and giveth.

37.13.1.en: 1- The wicked man is greedy; he is not content with what he has and borrows from those around him to satisfy his lusts, but because God's blessing is not with him he remains needy and is unable to repay what he borrowed, so he constantly feels deprivation, in addition to troubling those around him, for he takes from them and does not give to them, and this is what God's law declared by the hand of Moses (Deut 28:44).

37.13.2.en: 2- The wicked man has taken much from God, but he does not pay what he owes God, so he neither thanks God nor helps others; he always wants to take and not give, because he is selfish and refuses to do good.

37.13.3.en: 3- King Saul made use of David in killing Goliath, and as a military commander who defended his country against the Philistines, his enemies, but Saul did not thank him, but pursued him and tried to kill him throughout his life, until Saul died. Likewise Judas Iscariot took much from Christ and gave Him nothing in return, but on the contrary sold Him to the Jews for pieces of silver, and his end was destruction, because he was selfish. And the Jews benefited from Christ in His miracles, but did not thank Him, but rose up against Him and crucified Him, and they perished when the Romans destroyed Jerusalem in AD 70.

37.13.4.en: 4- The righteous children of God enjoy God's blessing even if what they have is little, and they thank God for it and are inclined to give, since their hearts are full of compassion for the poor, so they help and give to every needy person, and God's blessings to them increase, as the Law said (Deut 15:2).

37.13.5.en: Thank God for His gifts to you, and He will increase them for you so that you can help those around you. For God's gifts are not for you alone, but for all those around you, that is, that you may give from them to every needy person.

37.14.s.en: (3) The protection of the righteous is assured

37.14.0.en: 22- For such as be blessed of him shall inherit the earth; and they that be cursed of him shall be cut off.

37.14.1.en: 1- Whoever pleases God, He blesses him, so he inherits the earth, that is, he receives blessings and good things on earth, and thanks God for them, so He pours out on him many blessings, and thus he lives in God's blessing and thanksgiving.

37.14.2.en: 2- The one blessed by God inherits the earth, that is, he sees God on earth in all His gifts, so he enjoys fellowship with Him and possesses God, because he feels that God is the whole world, and he is the son of God, so he enters into His embrace, and sees Him in all the virtues of others and in all that is on earth, and so lives in constant joy.

37.14.3.en: 3- The one blessed by God inherits the new earth, which is the Kingdom of Heaven, because he lived faithfully on earth, so he deserves eternal life with Him.

37.14.4.en: 4- The wicked lose God's blessing, so nothing remains for them but the absence of blessing, that is, the curse; these are deprived of seeing God and feeling Him, so they are cut off from being in His presence, and live in the darkness of sin, which leads them to the darkness of eternal torment.

37.15.0.en: 23- The steps of a man are established by the LORD: and he delighteth in his way.

37.15.1.en: 24- If he fall, he shall not be cast down: for the LORD upholdeth him with his hand.

37.15.2.en: 1- God loves His children who hold fast to His commandments, so He helps them in their spiritual striving and establishes their steps on the way to the Kingdom.

37.15.3.en: 2- Because of God's fatherhood and love He does not leave anyone else to care for His children, but He Himself cares for them, because He alone knows the secrets of their hearts, and consequently knows what suits them; He feels with them and establishes them in His way however great the obstacles. For God is able to remove them, or to bring them over them.

37.15.4.en: 3- God rejoices greatly in His children's response to Him and their holding fast to Him, and God's joy in His righteous children gladdens them and drives them into greater striving to enjoy fellowship with Him.

37.15.5.en: 4- The children of God are exposed to temptations like the rest of mankind, but God does not let the temptation dominate them and cast them to the ground, so that they lose their ability to strive spiritually, but He stretches out His hand and supports them, that they may continue the way with Him to the Kingdom.

37.15.6.en: 5- The children of God are also exposed to falling into sin, but if they fall they take refuge in God by repentance, and He forgives them and supports them, so they are not cast down in sin and do not surrender to it. And by God's power they overcome sin, and even rush into greater striving that makes them grow in the love of God.

37.16.0.en: 25- I was young, and now am old; yet have I not seen the righteous forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.

37.16.1.en: 1- David offers a personal, practical experience, which is that the righteous children of God cannot be forgotten by God, but He cares for all their needs, and even provides for the needs of their children; for the blessing of the righteous extends to his offspring, so they are godly, and God blesses them, and they lack nothing.

37.16.2.en: 2- St. Augustine sees that David speaks with the tongue of the Church, which from its beginning was "young," and until the end of days "is now old," and God has not forsaken any of her righteous children nor their offspring.

37.16.3.en: 3- The righteous is the one who loved God and was occupied with Him, and so sought the heavenly Kingdom before anything else; God provides for his needs, his and his offspring's, as Christ declared this clearly in His Sermon on the Mount, "But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you" (Mt 6:33).

37.16.4.en: 4- God's care for the righteous is to satisfy him spiritually. And the bread that He gives to his offspring is the spiritual food, for this is more important than material food. Although God does not forget his material needs either.

37.16.5.en: 5- There are righteous men who have been hungry, such as Abraham and Isaac, who went to Gerar for bread (Gen 26:1), and Paul, who was exposed to hunger (2 Cor 11:27), but God did not forsake them, and they did not die of hunger.

37.16.6.en: 6- The righteous is distinguished by tenderness and compassion, for he feels the needs of those around him, and as God loved him he loves those around him, so he helps them, and if they need to borrow from him he lends to them.

37.16.7.en: 7- The whole life of the righteous is an occupation with doing good; his whole day he has compassion on those around him in different kinds of service, and indeed throughout his life he keeps doing good.

37.16.8.en: 8- The offspring of the righteous walk in the way of the Lord like him, so they receive the Lord's blessings in their lives, and also care to bless those around them, helping them and doing good with them.

37.17.0.en: 27- Depart from evil, and do good; and dwell for evermore.

37.17.1.en: 1- David declares that the characteristics of the children of God are two things, which are:

37.17.4.en: It is not enough to do one of these two commandments; the two commandments must be complete together in the life of the children of God. Whoever keeps away from evil only and does not do good is a person who does not show his sonship to God who loves goodness, and whoever does good and does not depart from evil is a person who limps between the two sides and is not a true son of God.

37.17.5.en: 2- The reward of the children of God who depart from evil and do good is the greatest reward, which is eternal life and dwelling in it, that is, settling forever in the Kingdom, in addition to God's blessings in this life, such as the grace of inward peace.

37.18.0.en: 28- For the LORD loveth truth, and forsaketh not his godly ones. They are preserved for ever: but the seed of the wicked shall be cut off.

37.18.1.en: 1- The Lord loves truth, which is virtue and the doing of good, and this is what the righteous and the just do; therefore God loves them and blesses them with many blessings.

37.18.2.en: 2- If Satan supports the wicked in doing evil, all the more God does not forsake His righteous children, so He blesses them in their life on earth with many blessings, and if they are exposed to sufferings in the present life, He compensates them for them with inexpressible glories in the Kingdom of Heaven.

37.18.3.en: 3- The wicked may flourish in the present life and enjoy some material things, but they have lost their peace, and then in the eternal life they are cut off from God's presence and cast into eternal torment.

37.18.4.en: 4- As for the righteous, they enjoy their life on earth in fellowship with God, and then inherit eternal life. By this we find the inheritance of the earth repeated six times for certain groups, namely: first, those who wait for the Lord and rely on Him (vv. 3, 9, 34), second, the meek (v. 11), third, the blessed (v. 22), and finally the righteous (v. 29). And we find that in the fourth time he mentioned the righteous, who are those marked by the three previous characteristics.

37.19.0.en: 30- The mouth of the righteous meditateth wisdom, and his tongue speaketh truth.

37.19.1.en: 1- Meditating is murmuring, that is, repeating a thought and a feeling about something, and this belongs to the heart, then appears on the mouth. The mouth of the righteous meditates wisdom, that is, his heart, his mind, his tongue and also all his works are marked by wisdom.

37.19.2.en: 2- Wisdom is the word of God, and its work by the Holy Spirit in man's heart appears in the tongue, then in works. So man speaks the word of God and the will and desire of God at all times.

37.19.3.en: 3- The truth is God, so whoever lives by wisdom, that is, the word of God, will of course speak the truth, that is, everything sound, and will declare God in his speech.

37.19.4.en: 4- This is the first time in the Book of Psalms that the word wisdom is mentioned, so whoever repeats the psalms much is filled with wisdom and speaks it.

37.19.5.en: 5- Man's mouth is an instrument for glorifying God, and therefore the Book of Psalms mentions the mouth and the tongue often (seventy-five times) to call the children of God to sanctify their tongues by repeating the words of God, so that Satan, who wants to use their tongues for evil, keeps away from them.

37.20.0.en: 31- The law of his God is in his heart; none of his steps shall slide.

37.20.1.en: 1- The heart of the righteous is occupied with God's Law, so he enjoys meditating on it, then it appears in his conduct, that is, his steps; he lives by God's Law, and whoever lives by it does not turn aside from God's way and is not shaken by the evils of the world, but walks with earnest steps toward his goal, which is the Kingdom.

37.20.2.en: 2- God's Law, that is, His commandments and judgments, is a support for man on his way to the Kingdom; it is not heavy on him or restricting of his steps, but on the contrary encourages him, leads him in God's way and fills him with inward peace.
